newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil steady on tight supply.

text.p: European straight-run markets were steady on Tuesday, with traders saying a combination of tighter supply and some buying interest were giving it support.

No deals were reported but sellers were at about the $101 mark while others were asking $2 or $3 a tonne higher for better quality material. One Brent-related bid was heard, the equivalent of $99 per tonne.
"The market is more long than short," one trader said.
Traders said some buying interest was coming into the low sulphur straight-run market especially from the United States.
"With the better contango, people want to buy to put into tanks," the trader added.
A second trader said he did see the market pushing below the $100 mark, adding the limited supplies resulting partly from the shutdown of a supplier's German refinery were supporting the market.

"I don't see anyone pushing it to $100 (a tonne)... simply because of the shutdown and there is no overhang in the market; all the big cargoes have moved to the States...No one is in a big hurry to sell," he said.
"If crude holds straight-run will hold," the trader added.
